title: Nightshift Passport: shift notes & action sketch
content:
Purpose:
Quick, freeform handoff for nightshift covering the 23:00-07:00 UTC window. Not a polished postmortem — a passport to pick up context fast. Include open questions in "Questions for next" so they don’t get lost.

TL;DR:
- Small but noisy latency surge in us-west-2 between 02:18–02:47 UTC; 95th p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms for generation requests.
- Root-cause candidate: KV-cache churn after an autoscaler bounce + a sudden spike of long-sequence inference (user test job).
- Manual mitigations applied: pinned pool-sized routing for high-latency customers, increased short-term cache TTL, and rolled back last autoscaler policy (rollout v2 -> v1).
- No customer-facing downtime; a couple of elevated customer support tickets opened for transient tail latency.

Timeline (rough):
- 02:12 UTC: Alerts start (latency_surge_us_west2 p95 > 300ms for 3m).
- 02:15 UTC: Pager to SRE; I (Priya) joined bridge.
- 02:18 UTC: Observed correlation to model-serving-host OOM churn on node group g2-serve-24 in us-west-2 (OOM kills then pod restarts).
- 02:22 UTC: Found a heavy client job (internal test harness) sending long context (~12k tokens) into redwood-7b-quant-prod; KV cache warmed & thrash observed, local KV memory ballooned leading to reclaim and GC pressure.
- 02:30 UTC: Applied routing override for tier-pinned customers to us-east-1 and eu-central-1 for latency-sensitive routes.
- 02:36 UTC: Temporarily increased kv-cache-ttl from 60s -> 300s for serving runtime in us-west-2 to reduce churn pressure while we stabilized.
- 02:40 UTC: Autoscaler rollout v2 reverted to v1 (recent autoscaler change included an aggressive scale-down that led to fragmenting long-lived KV allocations).
- 02:47 UTC onwards: p95 trended back toward baseline over 15 minutes.

Mitigations performed (explicit steps):
- Routing override:
  - Command: rdctl route override --region us-west-2 --route generation:* --destination us-east-1 --reason "latency mitigation 2026-03-13"
  - Note: this is temporary; must clear after shift if not needed.
- Cache TTL bump:
  - Edit config: /infra/serving/runtime/configs/kv-cache.yaml (ttl_seconds: 60 -> 300) then rollout: infractl apply --component serving-runtime --region us-west-2
  - Watch: memory_pressure and kv_cache_hit_rate (dashboard link above).
- Autoscaler rollback:
  - Rolled back deployment tag autoscaler:v2 -> autoscaler:v1. Command in PR linked above.

Observations + evidence to attach for postmortem:
- Pod kill logs: node g2-serve-24 had repeated OOM kills. Attach logs from 02:10–02:35 UTC.
- Heap/GC graphs: noticeable GC spikes concurrent with KV eviction events.
- Request trace sample: several long-context requests from internal-test-client-03 (trace ids listed in slack thread).
- Correlation: rollout of autoscaler:v2 yesterday at 18:00 UTC did gradual scale-down with shorter grace period -> more frequent pod churn.

Immediate follow-ups (owners & rough due dates):
- Capture and attach full log bundle to JIRA-2026 (INC-4127) (owner: Liam O'Connor) — due 2026-03-14
- Run controlled repro for long-context job to measure KV churn thresholds (owner: Zoe Chen) — start 2026-03-14
- Draft runbook section: "KV cache thrash" with decisions guardrails for TTL, per-route pinning, and autoscaler policies (owner: Priya Nair) — draft by 2026-03-16
- Add a canary check in infra CI to detect aggressive autoscaler scale-down (owner: Mateo Alvarez) — proposal by 2026-03-18

Runbook edits (quick notes for the draft):
- New check: on latency surge, first inspect kv_cache_free_bytes and kv_cache_eviction_rate (dashboard IDs: kv-001, kv-002).
- If eviction_rate > 5% for > 5m AND p95 > 300ms: do temporary TTL bump to 300s, then evaluate if routing is necessary.
- Add step: before autoscaler policy rollout, run offline simulation with 95th percentile long-seq traces (use repro harness in /tools/repro/long-seq).
- Add explicit rollback trigger: if pod_restarts > 3 in 10m for serving pods, abort autoscaler rollout and revert to previous stable image.

Customer & CS notes (what to tell affected customers):
- Impact: brief p95 latency increase from ~120ms -> up to ~420ms for a ~30m window. No request loss, no model degradation.
- Mitigation: we pinned traffic away from the affected region for latency-sensitive routes and stabilized cache TTLs.
- Follow-up: a technical note will be shared once we complete the root-cause write-up.

Questions for next oncall (do not skip):
- Confirm that routing override was cleared (if stable) or extended (if still needed). Command to clear: rdctl route override --clear --region us-west-2 --route generation:*
- Check memory_pressure graph for g2-serve-24 and any new OOMK events since 06:00 UTC.
- Has the internal-test-client-03 team scheduled repeated long-context jobs in the next 24h? If yes, coordinate to run on a non-production pool.

Notes to myself / rough ideas for longer-term fixes:
- Consider per-tenant KV quotas or soft-limits to avoid a single tenant blowing cache memory (tenant-level protectors).
- Smarter autoscaler: add knowledge of KV-residency (long-lived state) so scale-down avoids killing nodes with many hot KV entries.
- Pre-warm strategy: detect large long-context jobs and pre-warm ephemeral pools rather than letting them displace cached state.

Quick commands & links (copyable):
- Check p95 by region: dashboards.redwood.net/ops/latency?region=us-west-2
- Pod restart list: kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by='.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount' | tail -n 30
- Restart helper (do not use without pager): infractl restart nodegroup g2-serve-24 --region us-west-2 --grace 300

Housekeeping / handoff checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] Attach logs to INC-4127 (owner Liam)
- [ ] Confirm routing override state (owner next-oncall)
- [ ] Publish a short incident note to #ops-summary and link to JIRA (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Create runbook PR for "KV cache thrash" (owner: Priya)

Sign-off: Priya Nair (nightbridge) 2026-03-13 07:02 UTC

Appendix (raw snippets saved here for quick find):
- Sample trace ids: trace-eb34f9, trace-eb34fa, trace-eb3501 (internal-test-client-03).
- Pod logs excerpt (02:21:14 UTC): "OOMKilled: runtime/mem: attempted allocation ... kv-alloc-size=29G"
- Autoscaler rollout PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/201 (rolled back to infra@v1.9.2)

Freeform TODOs (notes to self):
- Think about a lightweight synthetic that pulses long-seq traffic to a staging pool every 6h so we detect regressions early.
- Coordinate with model-onboarding: warn them that redwood-7b-quant is sensitive to extreme long-context tests and provide a recommended test harness.
